Approximate conversions (°Bx ≈ °NM × 1.025, °Oe ≈ °NM × 4.25, 1 °NM ≈ 0.6 % vol). Your must meter or lab result wins.
Add %1$s kg sugar (%2$s per hl) → about %3$s %% vol

Theory: 1.0 kg sucrose per hl raises the must by 1 °NM. Growers often use 1.1–1.2 to be safe; your 2025 rosé note says 1.2 overshot, so 1.0–1.1 is likely right for you. Mind the legal enrichment limit for your zone.
Need %1$s mg/L free SO₂ (add %2$s mg/L) → %3$s g KMS for %4$s L, or %5$s mL of 10 %% solution
Molecular SO₂ = free SO₂ / (1 + 10^(pH − 1.81)). 0.5 mg/L is the usual target for dry whites, 0.8 mg/L for extra protection. KMS ≈ 57 % SO₂.
Add %1$s g tartaric acid (%2$s g/L). Expect pH to drop by about %3$s.
Add about %1$s g potassium bicarbonate (%2$s g/L) to lower TA by %3$s g/L; test on a sample first, part of the drop only comes after cold stabilisation.
1 g/L tartaric acid raises TA by ≈ 1 g/L and lowers pH by ≈ 0.1. KHCO₃ ≈ 1.2 g/L per 1 g/L TA reduction (0.67 g/L CaCO₃ does the same with more sediment).
Target ≈ %1$s mg/L YAN → deficit %2$s mg/L → about %3$s g/hl DAP (or organic nutrient per label, about 2–3× that)
YAN is sufficient for this potential alcohol.
Targets: ~200 mg/L up to 12.5 % vol, ~250 for 13–14 %, ~300 above. 1 g/hl DAP ≈ 2.1 mg/L YAN; EU cap 100 g/hl DAP. Split additions: a third at pitching, the rest at 1/3 sugar depletion.

Vineyard Log is a notebook for a small vineyard and cellar. Three things make everything else work:
Vineyard tab → +. Name, variety (pick from the catalogue), number of vines and the year planted. Then set the vineyard location in Settings so the weather, GDD and disease risk can be fetched.

Open a block and tap +: spray (products with dose per 10 l and PHI), fertilisation, phenology stage from photos, ripeness readings, harvest. In the cellar, create a batch from a block and log its steps.
The Overview tab shows the disease risk, the next reminders and open plan tasks, then the season charts. Reminders and daily alerts come on their own once you allow notifications.

When you need more: the field guide with growth stages and diseases, the spray programme, cellar protocol templates, the season plan, catalogue import and backup live behind the icons of each tab and in Settings.
Rain since 1 May: %1$s mm, last 7 days %2$s mm – the input of the Šteberla downy-mildew method (curves A/B are not public; see the BS weekly report).

Weekly infection-pressure ratings per station (Šteberla for downy mildew, Kast for powdery mildew, botrytis), product traffic light with PHI and a 7-day outlook, published by BS vinařské potřeby; amet.cz maps the Šteberla severity for South Moravia.
Since 1 May %1$s mm · curve A %2$s mm · curve B %3$s mm · %4$d rain days
Non-calamitous zone: only the basic sprays – before flowering, after flowering and before berry softening of early varieties.
Sporadic-calamitous zone: the basic sprays plus further ones at your discretion.
Calamitous zone: start protection at once and spray regularly as the vine grows, so new shoots, leaves, inflorescences and bunches stay covered.

Šteberla, Vančová, Valuš, Zeman: Agrometeorologická predpoveď peronospóry viniča, Meteorologické zprávy 35/1982 (SHMÚ, Malokarpatská oblast 1951–1975). A = maxima of non-calamitous years, B = minima of calamitous years, weekly sums from 1 May; used from 14 May to 30 July.
Šteberla evaluation starts on 14 May (rain 1–14 May).
Šteberla: cumulative rain %1$s mm since 1 May is above curve B (%2$s mm) – calamitous downy-mildew zone, keep the vine covered as it grows.
Forecast period ended on 30 July (berry softening of early varieties); the value shown is the final one.

BS spray plan 2025 (per litre of water):

From the BS 2025 plan: add sulphur (Kumulus, Solfernus) to every tank mix; in organic growing copper must stay under 4 kg Cu/ha/year in total; never mix concentrates – add each product to the tank separately and stir; fosetyl-Al not with SC products, sulphur or ammonium nitrogen; Karathane New at visible powdery mildew in any stage (0.05 %, max 4× a season); Vínofit for regeneration after frost, drought or hail.
Grams of metallic Cu per kg or litre (label: e.g. 500 g/kg for Kuprikol 50). Used for the 4 kg Cu/ha/year organic budget; parsed from the active ingredient when empty.

Three steps as in the BS technology sheets: complex nutrient at pitching (20 g/hl), a second dose when a third of the sugar is gone (10–20 g/hl), the last third gets 20–30 g/hl against stuck fermentation (30 for potential alcohol above 13.5 %). YAN target by potential alcohol.
